title: Benefits and Challenges of Four-day Work Week
what_it_is: Benefits and Challenges of Four-day Work Week

sections.label: Four-day work week feasibility
sections.summary: Ministry notes overseas four-day work week pilots and concerns, and encourages flexible work arrangements instead of commissioning its own study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry is aware of any ongoing studies being conducted by third parties to examine the feasibility of a four-day work week in Singapore; and (b) if not, whether the Ministry will consider this as a core issue and prioritise the commission of its own study to examine the benefits and challenges of a four-day work week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: We have noted reports of four-day work week pilots in other countries, such as Ireland, Japan and Spain.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Elsewhere, such as in Belgium, employees have the right-to-request for a four-day work week, but with daily work hours extended so that the total number of hours worked per week remains the same.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Some of the key concerns that stakeholders have include the impact on productivity, business costs and employee well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: While productivity improvements have been reported in some cases, this depends on sector and job type.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: In some instances, reduced work hours have had to be compensated by hiring more labour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: At the same time, employees are concerned that their salaries could be reduced due to fewer hours worked, while some could face increased stress when they work more hours than usual in a day to complete their work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: A four-day work week is one of many types of flexible work arrangements, and the Ministry, together with the tripartite partners, strongly encourage employers and employees to be open to flexible work arrangements in all its various forms to identify and adopt those that best suit their unique business needs and those of the workers.

sections.label: No imposed public sector trial
sections.summary: MOM does not intend to specify any trial or impose such formulas on the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: MOM does not intend to specify any trial or rigidity or impose any of these formulas on the public sector.
